references.text: The earth opened its mouth and swallowed Korah, Dathan, and Abiram with their households. This is a direct parallel to the image of the earth swallowing, used concerning God's judgment on his enemies.
Moses reminds the people how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed Dathan and Abiram. The same Hebrew expression for the earth swallowing is used here.
The psalmist mentions God's right hand and arm that gave Israel victory, reflecting the theme of God's right hand acting with power.
Refers to God's right hand leading Israel and driving out the nations, the same motif as in Exodus 15:12.
The Lord's right hand does great deeds and exalts, a recurring theme connected to God's mighty right hand in Exodus 15:12.
The Lord stretches out his hand against his people, and the mountains tremble. The image of God's outstretched hand in judgment is parallel.
God says he will stretch out his hand against Egypt. This is an earlier reference to God's outstretched hand against enemies.
Earlier in the same song, God's right hand is mentioned as crushing the enemy, a direct parallel within the same context.
Psalm 74:11 alludes directly to God's saving power in Exodus by asking that the same 'right hand' that struck down the enemies be brought forth again.
Korah's rebellion (Numbers 16) is the direct parallel to Exodus 15, where the earth opens up to swallow God's enemies.
A typological parallel where the earth opens its mouth to swallow the guilty (Cain/Abel and Pharaoh's army).
